newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's new farm minister likes supply management.
newsitem.headline: Canada's new farm minister likes supply management.

text.p: Canada's new agriculture minister, Lyle Vanclief, said on Wednesday he favored the continuation of the country's supply management programs.
Vanclief, chairman of the House of Commons Agriculture Committee, also said he envisioned staying the course set by his predecessor, Ralph Goodale.
"I don't see any major changes," Vanclief told reporters after being sworn in to the new Liberal cabinet, nine days after general elections.
Goodale became natural resources minister while retaining responsibility for the Canadian Wheat Board (CWB).

Canada runs a supply management program for dairy, eggs and poultry, which survived a U.S. challenge under the North American Free Trade Agreement. Production in Quebec and Saskatchewan is also supply-managed.
"I'm a very firm believer in supply management, but agriculture is an industry that has always evolved," Vanclief said.

"Supply-managed industry has evolved somewhat in the last few years. Evolution will take place in the industry...but I'm a firm believer supply management will be there for a lot longer than I'm around."
Vanclief, who served as parliamentary secretary for agriculture from 1993 to 1996, holds a degree in agriculture from the University of Guelph.
